A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CPT-PG research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–J support reliable comparison, including material relocated or reformatted in v5.

before.justification: V4 reports original simulations in Section 5 and Appendices F and J, including bandit, grid, financial trading, electricity-management, and MuJoCo results.

after.justification: V5 retains these original simulations, including learning curves, policy comparisons, and empirical return distributions.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the existing estimator specification: gain/loss samples are ordered separately, and each trajectory's estimated CPT weight enters its score-function contribution before averaging. V4's alternative piecewise-affine/quadratic approximation procedure in Appendix D.2 is removed. The core CPT-PG approach remains, and corresponding implementation changes are not established.

E1.justification: The evaluated coverage is retained: gain/loss bandits, grid environments, traffic control, electricity management, BTC-USD trading, and InvertedPendulum-v5. New theoretical policy-class results do not introduce an evaluated task or scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain vanilla PG and exponential risk-sensitive PG, CPT-SPSA-G in the grid-scaling comparison, and the same policy-class comparisons in Appendix J.4. Expanded discussion of other algorithms does not add evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Reported experimental settings remain unchanged, including trading dates, grid sizes, optimizers, learning rates, batch sizes, and training budgets. The growing-batch requirement introduced for theoretical convergence does not establish revised experimental protocols.

E4.justification: Both versions retain batch-size sensitivity in Figure 15, Markovian versus non-Markovian comparisons in Figure 17, utility/reference-point sensitivity in Figure 3, and the same application case studies. No new ablation or robustness analysis is reported.

E5.justification: Empirical uncertainty reporting is retained: Figure 1 uses five independent seeded runs with standard-deviation shading, Figure 3 reports medians and interquartile margins over ten runs, and Figure 15 uses 100 runs. No new empirical statistical procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: The empirical plots and corresponding findings are unchanged, including the bandit reflection effect, CPT-PG versus CPT-SPSA-G scaling, financial utility sensitivity, and appendix learning curves and return distributions. No changed empirical values, rankings, or result entries were found.

T1.justification: V5 adds reward-augmented Markov-policy sufficiency (Proposition 3), objective smoothness (Lemma 13), and total sample complexity of O-tilde(epsilon^-4) for approximate stationarity (Theorem 15), with proofs. It revises gain/loss definitions, the gradient and consistency proofs, concentration bounds, and asymptotic convergence assumptions, and adds a Hölder-continuity extension. The earlier fixed-batch convergence argument is replaced by an explicit growing-batch bias/noise analysis; the alternative approximation lemmas are removed.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list add a non-asymptotic total sample-complexity guarantee. V5 also withdraws v4's explicit claim that exact asymptotic convergence needs no increasing batch sizes, materially narrowing a central convergence claim while retaining the main CPT-PG and simulation contributions.

C2.justification: V5 identifies finite-sample estimator bias where v4 asserted unbiasedness. It adds substantive qualifications about endpoint-singular weighting functions, finite state-action theory, and conjectural infinite-horizon extensions. It also explains why the retained ordinary-Markov-policy comparison does not contradict the new reward-augmentation sufficiency result.

D1.justification: Remark 18 newly specifies that the limited-history experiments used at most one preceding state and points to supplementary code for network architectures. This adds documentation without establishing rerun experiments. Hardware, software, data-access information, and numerical hyperparameters are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: Sections 3.2 and 6 substantially expand positioning against Vijayan and L.A. (2024), Markowitz et al. (2023), and Pachal et al. (2025), distinguishing objectives, finite-sample estimators, and guarantees. V5 also adds Wang et al. (2025) and Kitamura et al. (2026), while removing the PyTorch reference.

P1.justification: The main seven-section sequence and Appendices A–J remain. Targeted prose revisions affect the utility explanation, estimator exposition, contributions, related work, and conclusion; proof subsections are retitled or reorganized, and author and acknowledgment text is updated.

P2.justification: V5 adopts TMLR formatting throughout, changing typography, running headers, text width, and figure sizes and placement. Figures 5–7, 14, and 16 include redrawn vector diagrams. The MuJoCo hyperparameter table remains but loses its numbered caption. These are substantial presentation changes despite retained empirical plots.

improvement.justification: V5 substantially repairs a central deficiency: v4 claims an unbiased estimator and fixed-batch exact convergence, whereas v5 corrects the estimator specification and supplies an explicit growing-batch bias/noise analysis. The finite-time guarantee and reward-augmentation theorem further strengthen the theoretical contribution, with clearer applicability limits. These gains outweigh the removal of the optional approximation discussion and some smaller plot layouts; the empirical evidence is retained.
